notes: Offscreen Qt uses software rasterization; absolute drag latency is not comparable to a GPU desktop session. Compare the relative open/closed regression instead.
The offscreen QFontDatabase has no font directory, so card text rasterization may be cheaper than on a desktop session.
A cold switch resets the whole ThumbnailProvider generation before the sample; a warm switch reuses the warmed LRU.

Batch switching uses the public list selection path. Each navigation sample waits for a paint of the correct selected target with enabled, non-loading canvas and matching batch and card selection. A mismatched target or timeout aborts the harness rather than becoming a fast passing sample.
Each drag sample is one synthetic mouse move plus one event loop turn; each drag moves the box by five screen pixels and releases it, which triggers the production card refresh.
The host may run unrelated work concurrently; every condition is repeated three times and the threshold uses the p95 of all 90 samples, with per-repeat p95 reported.
Image entries are bounded by the provider LRU (limit_entries); the probe shows the plateau.
latest_requests/card_request_keys are one small tuple per visited object, not per switch or per pixel; start_generation clears them.
The provider has no source-pixel cache: crop_thumbnail opens the image file once per request on a worker thread.

image_lifecycle.method: normal load_file, two images, two outputs, close/reopen
image_lifecycle.memory_note: RSS includes Qt/allocator caches; inspect warm trace for growth separately from discrete cache limits.

source_pixels.thumbnail_source_cache: none; crop_thumbnail re-opens the image file for each request
